newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Gaddafi asks Syria to use force to "liberate" Golan.
newsitem.headline: Gaddafi asks Syria to use force to "liberate" Golan.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi on Friday called on Syria's army to attack and take back the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights "today before tomorrow".
Gaddafi also urged the Lebanese army to join pro-Iranian guerrillas fighting to drive Israeli troops from an occupied border strip in south Lebanon.

"The Syrian army must enter the Golan and liberate it by force," the Libyan leader told a news conference at the end of a five-day visit to Tunisia. "Lebanon must also advance and liberate the occupied zone."
The Golan Heights, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, is the main issue on the negotiating table between Israel and Syria.
Talks between the two countries have been suspended since March and tensions have risen recently with each side accusing the other of preparing for war.

"Israel occupied the Golan in 1967. It was about 30 years ago. It took a great (act of) patience from Syria to not have used its right to liberate its land, but the Israelis think that since Syria didn't resist, they can keep the Golan," Gaddafi said.
"Today before tomorrow, the Golan must be liberated and Arabs will all fight with her (Syria)," he said.
"The Lebanese army and people must fight in south Lebanon not only Hizbollah," Gaddafi added.
Hizbollah (Party of God) is launching a guerrilla war against Israeli and allied forces occupying a border strip that runs upto 15 km (nine miles) into Lebanese territory.
